niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, geography, creative needs, and whether you want programmatic buying, direct-sold inventory, cross‑platform measurement, etc. That said, here’s a quick way to pick and some high-quality options by category.

How to choose an agency (quick checklist)
- Primary objective: brand awareness, direct response/DR, audience-building, or linear+streaming attribution?
- Buying preference: programmatic DSPs vs. direct buys with publishers (Roku, Hulu, Peacock)?
- Measurement needs: third‑party measurement, cross‑platform attribution, brand lift?
- Creative needs: do you need bespoke CTV creative and interactive units?
- Data & targeting: first‑party data ingestion, household/people‑based targeting, data partnerships?
- Scale & geography: US-only vs. global reach.
- Budget: large holding groups handle big buys; specialists can be more cost-effective for mid-market.
- Transparency & fraud prevention: viewability, invalid traffic controls, certified partners.

Reputable players (by role)
- Global media holding groups (full-service, scale, cross‑platform planning): GroupM (Wavemaker/Mindshare), Omnicom Media Group (OMD/PHD), Publicis Media (Starcom/Spark Foundry), IPG Mediabrands (UM/Initiative), Dentsu (Carat/iProspect). Good for big brands wanting integrated TV+digital plans.
- Programmatic/platforms (buying/activation + measurement partners): The Trade Desk (DSP), Roku/OneView (publisher DSP), Xandr (where available), Magnite, Tremor Video. These are tech platforms used by agencies and in-house teams.
- CTV specialists and measurement/activation firms: Simulmedia (cross‑screen TV planning), VideoAmp (measurement + activation), Cadent (audience targeting across linear/CTV), Innovid (creative/ad serving & measurement). Good for TV-first or performance-driven CTV.
- Independent performance agencies and consultancies: Tinuiti, Media.Monks, Merkle — often strong on data-driven activation and creative production for CTV.

When to pick each type
- Large national/global campaigns and complex cross‑channel measurement: use a global holding group or a top programmatic partner plus measurement vendor.
- Mid-market or performance-focused campaigns: choose a specialist programmatic CTV agency or an independent with proven ROAS case studies.
- If you need TV+linear planning and attribution: consider Simulmedia, Cadent, or a holding‑group team with TV specialists.
- If creative/interactive CTV units are critical: Innovid or Media.Monks plus a DSP integration.

Next step I can help with
- If you tell me: budget range, campaign goal (brand lift vs. conversions), geography, and whether you need creative/measurement, I’ll recommend 2–3 agencies/platforms tailored to your needs and a short RFP template to vet them. Which of those details can you share?
